uncertain.note: Division level plus a few brigades; regiments, battalions and the Luftwaffe/naval/Allied air orders of battle omitted (not retrieved). German 7th Army, Panzer Group West and Army Group B headquarters omitted (no positions). 70th Tank Battalion and the airborne regiments are inside their divisions.

US 2nd, 3rd Armored (landing date not retrieved), 8th Infantry Divisions and 2nd Infantry; British 79th Armoured, 4th Canadian Armoured (July, date not retrieved), Polish, French and Belgian units; German 2nd Panzer, 116th Panzer, 346th, 353rd, 77th and 85th Infantry Divisions, 102nd and 503rd Heavy Panzer Battalions (no arrival dates in M18). These were omitted rather than invented.

Approximate sector anchors (G03); no source gives division coordinates. Beach arrivals use the beach coordinates (M14/M15); airborne drop zones, German start areas and German arrival areas are inferred from the named sectors in M01-M12.

Airborne 01:00 and seaborne 06:30-08:00 on 6 June are approximate, and local time versus UTC is not resolved (G01). Follow-on arrivals use the sourced day (M16, M17, M18) at 12:00. 15th Scottish is set to 26 June 00:00 (Epsom start) as a latest-possible date; 43rd Wessex at 20 June (recce regiment off Sword); 59th Division and the Guards Armoured at the end of June; 1st SS, 2nd SS (midpoint of 15-30 June) and 10th SS dates are approximations of the sourced windows.

Game-scale (G01), except the sourced figures: 352nd about 12,000, 716th about 6,000, Panzer Lehr 208 tanks and assault guns. Rangers (9 companies), commandos and tank brigades have game-scale manpower.

Utah 1% (197 of 21,000, M03) and Omaha 7% (2,400 of 34,000, M04) are derived from sourced counts; Gold/Juno/Sword 3% casualties, and for airborne drops 12% casualties, 20 km dispersion, 18 penalty hours and organisation 40 (drops were scattered, M09), are game-scale (G01).

Arromanches throughput 6,000 t/day is the sourced achieved rate (M02); Mulberry A at 6,000 t/day is half the 12,000 t/day planning requirement (M08) and is game-scale. Availability from hour 192 (D+8, per team-lead from sources) with a 48 h ramp is game-scale; the storm cuts Mulberry A to 0.1 (abandoned, M08) and no repair step is modelled (no sourced repair date). Beach depots have small game-scale supplyCapacity 8. Mulberry B is not damaged by the storm event (M08 says it survived).
besiegedShare 0.8 on both Mulberries is a game-scale modelling choice (G01): sea-fed artificial harbours keep most of their throughput when German units are near; no source gives a figure.
Cherbourg is unusable as a supply port until 16 July (M02), then ramps over 240 h (game-scale). Its capture date is 26 June (M02) or 27 June (M11); both are recorded and the event uses 26 June.

Sourced as a fact (M01: 9,543 Allied against 815 Luftwaffe aircraft; M02: 4,029+5,514 against 570), but radius 80 km and speed multiplier 0.7 are game-scale (G01). No interdiction numbers were retrieved.

Charnwood (raid before dawn 8 July, time and aim point approximate), Goodwood (18 July, aim near Cagny) and Cobra (25 July, aim midway between Saint-Lo and Periers) positions, radii and casualty rates are approximate/game-scale; only the days are sourced (M11).
Utah is a Nominatim hamlet near Sainte-Marie-du-Mont, Gold a Nominatim guidepost, Omaha/Juno/Sword Wikipedia coordinates; positions are approximate and nudged to land.

Allied supply sources are the English embarkation ports Southampton, Portsmouth, Poole, Weymouth and Newhaven (positions from Wikipedia, M14); their throughputs (6,000/4,000/2,000/2,000/2,000 t/day) are game-scale (G01), not sourced. The beaches, Mulberries and Port-en-Bessin are Allied-owned from the start but are not sources (sea-fed). German sources are Lisieux, Falaise and Vire (rear towns, game-scale roles). Only Arromanches 6,000 t/day is a sourced tonnage. England is one coarse GBR initialControl box (G04).
captureBlockKm 6.5 (default 4) is a modelling flag (G01): a garrison on the outskirts of a town still holds it against an unopposed capture. Not a historical datum.

seaSupply: true and weatherControl.stormScale 0 are modelling flags (G01): every coastal port/depot a side holds is a supply source so the beachhead is supplied across the sea, and random storms are off because the Great Storm of 19-22 June is scripted (M01, M08). Neither is a historical datum.
Qualitative profile (game-scale). Sourced weather: the 19-22 June storm (M01), poor weather cancelling Epsom bombers and delaying Cobra (M11).
Game-scale (G01). All hold objectives credit only at the end date.
One German polygon over the whole map, small Allied boxes at the beaches, one over southern England.
